findings.summary: Dev-note is internally inconsistent about its own test count: line 39 says 15 new tests while line 114 says 14. The test file contains 15 it(...) blocks, so line 114 is the wrong figure. Cosmetic; it does not affect R7, whose 487 total is consistent with baseline 472 plus 15 new tests.

Dev-note records input_commit = 226aa5d404ad12c6de9a2d150638e37fd8d5ec82, which matches none of the identities visible to this review (dispatch input_commit ac147a8e, implementation handoff 75397fa2, prior attempt RF subject 71481f09). As a read-only reviewer I cannot resolve what the Implementer stage was actually dispatched with, so I record this as unverified rather than incorrect. Documentation only; the deterministic seal verifies HEAD against the dispatch input_commit independently, and spec section 4 point 3 forbids extra commits to align hashes.

The R1 discriminant needs 30 successive 10ms polls to complete inside a 500ms budget (~330ms expected), leaving roughly 170ms of headroom. The margin is adequate and the suite is reported green at 6.89s, but a heavily loaded runner could push the 31st read past the deadline and turn this into an intermittent failure. Raising AGENT_RESULT_TIMEOUT_MS for this one case would remove the timing coupling without weakening the kill of mutation S1.

Dev-note row S3 describes the killed assertion as 'R3a's expect(promise).rejects.toThrow(...)', but R3a is written as try/catch plus expect.fail; the rejects.toThrow form is used by R2c. The mutation is still genuinely killed (a null return makes runChannelWrite resolve and expect.fail fires), so only the wording of the mechanism is loose.
